Race conditions and state corruption when spawning/dismissing agents mid-pipeline while other agents hold file locks or are mid-edit

complexity_assessment.reasoning: Straightforward configuration file addition with clear requirements (doubled timeouts, opus-only routing, disabled features), CLI flag support, and test validation. Well-scoped, additive change with low architectural risk.

skill_rationale.architecture-design: Understanding Shipwright's template system architecture and how configuration overrides cascade through stages is essential to designing an emergency template that reliably applies all conservative settings without side effects.
skill_rationale.documentation: Reviewing existing template documentation patterns ensures the emergency template integrates consistently with current CLAUDE.md conventions and prevents operator confusion about when to use standard vs emergency templates.
skill_rationale.api-design: The CLI flag for `--template emergency` must follow Shipwright's existing interface conventions (e.g., similar to `--pipeline-template`, consistent argument ordering) to avoid cognitive load and maintain CLI consistency.
skill_rationale.testing-strategy: Test suite must validate that all conservative overrides (2x timeouts, opus-only effort routing, checkpoint_every_iteration, +50% iterations/restarts) are correctly applied by the template system and interact correctly with stage-level configurations.
skill_rationale.two-stage-review: Two-pass review ensures both technical correctness (template structure, overrides apply correctly) and strategic correctness (conservative settings actually improve reliability without wasting resources or creating new failure modes).
skill_rationale.pr-quality: Clear PR description explaining the emergency template's purpose, when to use it (repeated failures, high-priority issues), cost implications (opus-only), and limitations (no auto-merge, verbose logging overhead) is critical for operator decision-making.
skill_rationale.adversarial-quality: Challenge whether ultra-conservative settings actually improve success rate or just hide failures under extended timeouts; test edge cases like pathological scenarios where 2x timeouts still fail, and verify opus-only routing doesn't create new bottlenecks.
skill_rationale.validation-thoroughness: Real-world smoke tests running actual pipelines with the emergency template must confirm it achieves claimed reliability improvements, and measure the cost/time trade-offs compared to standard template for honest operator evaluation.

review_focus: Timeout multipliers: verify 2x standard values are both appropriate for reliability and reasonable for operator workflows (no pathological delays)
Model routing mechanics: confirm effort_level overrides actually force opus for all stages, and document token cost impact in CLAUDE.md
Checkpoint strategy: validate checkpoint_every_iteration provides recovery value without bloating state artifacts
CLI integration: ensure --template emergency works across all pipeline invocation patterns (pipeline start --issue, --goal, daemon mode)
Test coverage: verify tests cover all conservative settings and their interactions (e.g., high iteration count + checkpoint_every_iteration)
Documentation clarity: emergency template use case, cost warnings, and trade-offs must be unambiguous so operators choose it intentionally
Backward compatibility: adding new template must not affect existing template loading, selection logic, or CLI argument parsing
risk_areas: Timeout doubling could mask real code issues by allowing broken tests to time out instead of fail-fast with diagnostic output
Opus-only routing increases token costs dramatically—uncontrolled emergency template usage could exhaust daily budget or incur unexpected charges
No auto-merge leaves PRs in pending state indefinitely, requiring manual merge—could become operational bottleneck if template is used frequently
Disabling intelligence/prediction layers removes anomaly detection and cost optimization, potentially missing signals that standard template would catch

Template override mechanism complexity: ensure all 8 conservative settings (timeouts, effort, checkpoint, iterations, restarts, logging, intelligence, auto-merge) are correctly applied; partial application creates false reliability claims
Increased max_iterations without corresponding debugging improvements may not actually increase reliability—need to measure success rate delta empirically in validation
